photo_gallery.title: بيوت غدامس القديمة من الأعلى.jpg
photo_gallery.description:
Old town of Ghadames from above. One of UNESCO World Heritage Site in Libya
These houses, crafted from mud and palm wood, are tightly interconnected, resembling beehives. They feature a distinctive architectural style inspired by ancient Amazigh palace designs, constructed vertically. The ground floor is reserved for storing essential supplies, the first floor serves as the family’s living space, and the open rooftop is designated for women. Elevated passageways link the rooftops, allowing women to move freely while remaining out of sight from men.
